# Legacy Tripoli parity on the real BSU data

Generated by `scripts/tripoli_parity.py`: 31 distinct content hashes, 33 top-level workbooks, 126 pasted ratio references. Elapsed 1.236 s; slowest project parse 0.0265 s.

## Method and limits

Drive inputs were opened read-only. No raw files, cycle values or masks are embedded in this report or repository. Projects are deduplicated by SHA-256 (equivalent distinct set to SHA-1 here); top-level copies take precedence. SourceFileInfo, never the project filename, chooses the workbook. No project in this set serializes a combined-run source list. The unrelated source in KG5_z7_Pb.trip is unavailable, so its raw-reader parity cannot be claimed.

The safe MS-NRBF parser only constructs inert data. It follows [Microsoft MS-NRBF](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-nrbf/5acd9dc4-1439-433a-8d53-eb2922a142d8). Field/statistical interpretations were checked against OGTripoli source/RawRatio.cs (GetObjectData, Ratios setter, CalcStats, SetBlockOutliers), TripoliWorkProduct.cs, RunParameters.cs and forms/frmRatioGraph.cs. These are independent implementations of the format and numerical methods.

The actual streams are Tripoli 4.10.0.3. Positive signed Ratios are accepted; negative values are hand/rule discards, zero means missing. ActiveRatiosMap is a display cache. No AcceptedFlags or independent block flags are stored: block rejection changes signs too. Audit views add only verified zero padding to incomplete U blocks, and independently compute the in-place legacy oxide functions from workbook inputs. The public Analysis/replay API restores settings and individual ratio rejections as strict, undoable session history; no shared-mask union or new automatic rule is applied.

**Stored statistics are All* original/unfiltered statistics. Accepted statistics and block means are not serialized.** “Reconstructed accepted” rows compare Analysis against an independent scalar implementation of legacy CalcStats on the signed project data. They are algorithm checks, not independent stored results. The BSU pasted means/1σ %SE provide the independent accepted-statistic reference. StatsDetailDisplay=3 plots the mean ±2 SD band, alongside ±1 SD and ±1 SE. Reconstructed 2σ SD bands are explicitly labeled; this setting does not double clipboard %SE. No stored per-block statistics exist to validate in these files.

## Tolerances

Raw cycle comparisons use maximum absolute difference ≤ 2e-13 × maximum magnitude; ordinary source columns match exactly, while Decimal oxide arithmetic can round differently from float64. Means use 2e-12 relative tolerance, counts are exact. SD/SE/%SE additionally allow the standard naive-summation error bound: 8 γ_n (mean(x²)+mean(x)²)/sample_variance relative, with γ_n=n ε/(1−n ε), ε=float64 epsilon. This accounts for cancellation in legacy (Σx²−(Σx)²/n)/(n−1); the engine retains stable centered variance. The bound depends on n and coefficient of variation, not a fitted global cutoff. Clipboard comparisons add half a unit in the eighth significant digit, because C# E7 has eight significant digits. Numerical round-off within these bounds is classified as statistic definition/clipboard precision; it is not an engine defect.

## Findings for Phase 2

- TUNING Multiplier (Daly) dead time: [36.3] ns; recorded Multiplier gain: [1.0].
- CTRL (Apply Baselines, Correct for STDBL, Correct for BLKBL): [(True, True, True)]. CYCLE values are already processed; no extra dead-time/baseline/gain correction was applied by this audit.
- All 14 U projects record r18=0.0020, AmOxideCorrected=true, and separate inactive OxideCor functions. All retain the active workbook 0.00206 functions used in the pasted sheets. The active functions must continue to pass through without a second correction.
- All projects record Chauvenet threshold 0.5. Of 145 active functions, 144 have HandleOutliersFlag=1 (2σ); KG5 z7 U 238/233 oxide has Manual=0. Masks differ per ratio. A final mask does not establish the order of hand edits or the number of rule passes. Legacy 2σ is one pass on currently accepted positive values; legacy Chauvenet repeatedly rejects the worst point and recomputes (unlike Java one-pass/minimum-20 Chauvenet). This audit replays selections, not rejection algorithms.
- No project records applied fractionation or BaPO2/Tl correction; tracer/interference-use flags are false and alphaPb is zero. Capability flags can be true without an applied correction.
- Every U workbook has 270/267 equal to 270 intensity. Independent checks establish that the named 0.00206 columns use the correct physical ratio path through 270/265. The inactive legacy OxideCor functions reproduce correction of the mislabeled intensity at 0.0020; those are not the pasted ratios. This is an upstream workbook/input issue, not evidence to change the engine oxide formula.
- The two distinct nested Pb projects are reruns: KG5 z4 (57 cycles) and KG5 z7 (150 cycles). Their pasted means/errors match. The earlier top-level projects use 19 and 38 cycles respectively; their sheet discrepancies reflect different acquisitions, not a failed raw reader.
- KG5_z7_Pb.trip stores B1609_F12_GA9683326 z3 Pb-56377.xls as its only source (228 cycles, 32 functions), despite KG5/z7 labels. That workbook is absent. There is no evidence in its serialized source information for a concatenation of the two KG5 runs. Its internal statistics can be checked, but its workbook parity and identity remain unresolved.
